specification_compliance: I1: backend/app/services/fileops.py:492-498 deletes the moved file's CollectionItem rows whose collection drive != dst_drive. The delete is guarded on dst_drive != src_drive and runs before commit, so a move within one drive leaves items untouched.

I3: backend/app/database.py:561-584 runs the cleanup last in _migrate, after the playlists copy at :280-301. It runs only when files, collections and collection_items all exist, deletes only rows where files.drive <> collections.drive, logs INFO only when rowcount is non-zero, and catches exceptions so startup does not stop.

I4/I5/I6: backend/app/routers/internal.py:399-439 checks the nanoid (400), then the unknown drive (404 'Drive not found'), then the collection scoped to the drive (404 'Collection not found'). It filters on File.drive == drive and active_file_filter(), orders by position then id, and is gated by verify_internal_secret.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The cleanup's except branch logs at ERROR and continues. I3 does not say what should happen when the cleanup fails; the code comment argues that the read-side filters make the leftover rows harmless.
regression_risks: Rows with a NULL files.drive or NULL collections.drive are not deleted by the startup cleanup, because the <> comparison yields NULL. This is likely harmless if both columns are NOT NULL in the schema.
